questions.question: What can happen if you don't drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air builds up in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks collect water and oil. If you don't drain them, the water can freeze in cold weather and cause your brakes to fail.

questions.question: As a truck driver, you are responsible for all of the following, except:

options.text: Noticing if the weight is poorly balanced.
Knowing all fire department phone numbers along your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing all fire department phone numbers along your route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your cargo, check for poor weight balance, and make sure it is secure and doesn't block your view. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it. You are not required to memorize fire department numbers.

questions.question: When you start an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, check the gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal level within just a few seconds.

questions.question: If a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is broken:

options.text: The vehicle will have no brakes.
The vehicle will still brake normally.
The vehicle will go faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will still brake normally.
questions.explanation: The ABS system only prevents wheel lockup. If it breaks, your regular brakes still work. You can drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: When loading cargo, where should you place the weight?
questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Place weight as low as possible to keep the center of gravity low. This prevents your vehicle from tipping over.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: By waiting.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to let time pass and let your body process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, you should not:

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services to report the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a service station.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are classified as Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: While driving, what is allowed regarding text messages?

options.text: You cannot write texts, but you can read them.
You can write texts, but you cannot read them.
You cannot write or read texts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot write or read texts.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is not allowed. This includes writing text messages or reading them.

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you must back up, you should:

options.text: Get out and walk around to check the area.
Avoid using both side mirrors because they distract you.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can copy them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to check the area.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, always get out and look at the area. Check that you have enough space on the sides and above your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan realistic travel times.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. This reduces frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving: drive at safe speeds, keep safe distance from other cars, don't make angry gestures, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal
The distance your vehicle travels from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance your vehicle travels from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels between the moment you realize you must brake and the moment you actually press the brake pedal.

questions.question: What is true about a fatigued driver?

options.text: Usually more careful than other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: May react slowly to dangers
questions.explanation: Tired drivers see and react to hazards slower than alert drivers. Drowsy driving hurts your ability to make important decisions quickly.

questions.question: Before driving, check that your pedals:

options.text: Have grooves that are not worn smooth

questions.correctAnswerText: Have grooves that are not worn smooth
questions.explanation: Before your trip, check that nothing blocks the pedals and they work properly. Make sure the pedal surfaces are grooved for grip.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the storage tanks
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the storage tanks
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the governor decides when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force from the springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When should you sign a vehicle inspection report?
questions.correctAnswerText: After defects are fixed
questions.explanation: Sign the inspection report only if problems were found and either repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use the parking brake
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What must happen before air pressure falls below 55 psi in an air brake tank?

options.text: The warning light must turn on
The vehicle will not shift gears

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light must turn on
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must activate before pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning does not work during inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Should be expected on the roadway.
May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. A cardboard box may look harmless, but it could contain something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest speed is:

options.text: The same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: Which one is not a type of distraction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Obtuse
questions.explanation: Distractions are physical (reaching for an object), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (using a hand-held phone). Obtuse is not a type of distraction.

questions.question: When driving downhill, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle downhill and makes it go faster.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Warm up the vehicle so fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both systems before driving.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems. Check the air pressure gauges to watch the pressure.

questions.question: A steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with one hand while the other rests.
Held with both hands for a firm grip.
Released if the vehicle hits a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: Held with both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop:

options.text: The vehicle should shift to the right.
The vehicle should be in third gear.
The vehicle should not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when starting from a stop. Rolling back could hit something behind you.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.correctAnswerText: One-way check valve
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard:

options.text: You may drive onto the shoulder.
You should steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: A front brake limiting valve usually has two markings that read:
questions.correctAnswerText: "Normal" and "slippery."
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system does what?

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
Lubricates parts of the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that puts alcohol into the system. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the system.

questions.question: How can you prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move forward from a stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: Partially engage the clutch.
questions.explanation: With a manual transmission, you can partially engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal. This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving forward from a stop.

questions.question: What happens when you start an engine?

options.text: Warning lights turn on, then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on, then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, there may be a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: What are air tank drains used for?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and oil. If this builds up, it can damage the system. Drain valves on air tanks remove this water and oil.

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is most common at night because people are naturally less alert during hours when they normally sleep. Take precautions to avoid fatigue if you must drive at night.

questions.question: What must a truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Is using a hand-held mobile device while driving allowed?

options.text: Yes, if weather conditions are clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What must be done before transporting an over-length load?

options.text: Alert fire departments along the route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special transit permits.
questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads may need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, what should you check about the belt?
questions.correctAnswerText: That it is properly tightened.
questions.explanation: Before each drive, check the air compressor drive belt. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, hydroplaning risk increases if tire pressure is too low or tread is worn. If you start to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: When it is hard to see and you are driving near other vehicles, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving near other vehicles in poor visibility. This includes dawn, dusk, and bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction. This applies to any vehicle you drive. Parking violations are the exception.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: The air brakes should be used.
The vehicle should be placed in a low gear and the driver should use engine braking.
The driver should continually downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should be placed in a low gear and the driver should use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use engine braking in a low gear to slow down. Use your brakes only to help with engine braking.

questions.question: The heavier a vehicle is:

options.text: The less important the brakes become.
The harder the brakes need to work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes need to work.
questions.explanation: A heavier vehicle requires the brakes to work harder to stop it completely.

questions.question: If a truck has a trailer brake hand valve, it can be used to:

options.text: Prevent the truck from rolling back when being started from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the truck from rolling back when being started from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve stops the truck from rolling backward when you start from a complete stop.

questions.question: Which of these shows aggressive driving?

options.text: Slow down and maintain a reasonable following distance.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, and never making hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: When doing a pre-drive inspection, what should you do with the previous inspection report?

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
The inspection report must only be reviewed if there will be passengers in the vehicle.
The previous inspection report should be reviewed, if applicable.

questions.correctAnswerText: The previous inspection report should be reviewed, if applicable.
questions.explanation: Always review the last inspection report as your first step. Only sign a new report if any noted defects have been fixed.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three separate braking systems: service, parking, and emergency. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Consists of two separate air brake systems that share a single set of controls.
Is a single air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Consists of one air brake system for the left side of the truck and one system for the right side of the truck, each with its own set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Consists of two separate air brake systems that share a single set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems that share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually works the rear axle brakes, and the other works the front axle brakes.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, when does air pressure enter the brake chambers to move the rods and slack adjusters?
questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.
